mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns. The signal is the current level of FEDFUNDS, with lower values predicting positive returns.
failure_condition: Rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is non-negative (>=0) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions and imminent economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as investors price in recession risks.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises >0.3pp in 3 months, 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as market participants anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and HOUST (both falling in the same month) is associated with positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in industrial production signals a weakening economy, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as investors fear a hard landing.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, a decline in INDPRO is associated with positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above the 3-month moving average signals robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns as market participants react to near-term earnings momentum.
failure_condition: When RSAFS rises above the 3-month moving average, 5-day SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months indicates a persistent supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls >0.5% in 3 months, 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over three months signals rising inflation pressures, prompting monetary tightening expectations that cause negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises >0.2pp in 3 months, 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 10% over three months signals weakening consumer confidence and demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns as market participants react to immediate economic weakness.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls >10% in 3 months, 5-day SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.
